messages:
sam: Filing a POC blocker for Acme. They completed the security questionnaire and are ready, but their Hosted API key wasn't created and the Dedicated pool access isn't showing for their user. They can SSO into console but no tenant roles.

maria: Which provisioning flow did they set up? Okta SAML + SCIM or only SAML assertions? Also did they upload our SAML metadata or vice-versa?

sam: They say both enabled. Okta app name RDW-Acme-POC. We asked for the SAML metadata earlier and they confirmed exchange happened. SCIM service account exists but membership sync seems off.

kevin: Typical: Okta can either push groups (SCIM Group Push) or we infer groups from SAML claims. If group membership is missing in SCIM, auto-created API keys that depend on group->role mapping won't fire. Can you paste the SCIM provisioning debug link?

sam: I shared the provisioning logs link with them. Their Okta admin posted "success" events but our SCIM shows Group PUTs without members.

okta-bot: Provisioning log: 2024-09-05T09:41:02Z GRP_PUSH RDW-Acme-POC group=acme_poc_admin status=200 members=0

lee-idp: Also check Okta push filter: if they used a regex or prefix filter that excludes the group's exact displayName (case sensitive) it will create the group resource on our side but not attach members, depending on how Okta resolves membership during initial push.

nora-cs: Security note: We can't create API keys for users without written consent (per policy). If they want a manual key while fix is in progress, we need an email from an authorized Acme approver.

kevin: While waiting for approval, workaround is to backfill membership server-side: we can call our internal reconcile that queries SCIM /Users to see user->group relationships and populate Group.members if missing. That requires an admin op. Ops, are we allowed to do backfills for POCs?

maria: Ops will do backfills sparingly. Ask customer to try a manual Group Push in Okta Admin UI: App > Provisioning > Push Groups > Select acme_poc_admin > Push. Also verify the SCIM service account has Group.ReadWrite and Member.ReadWrite scopes.

sam: Acme says they did "assign users" to the app but unclear if they've pushed groups. I'll have them try a manual push and send the admin approval for temp key if needed. Also they asked if Private VPC Dedicated customers require any extra SAML config.

lee-idp: For Private/VPC customers we require SAML audience and ACS endpoints to match the private console URL. If their SAML config uses hosted.redwood.com but their dedicated console is at console.acme.internal, they need a second app or updated metadata. That mismatch can result in successful SSO but role mapping failures.

okta-bot: Provisioning log: 2024-09-05T09:46:10Z GRP_PUSH RDW-Acme-POC group=acme_poc_admin status=200 members=1 payload_members=1

kevin: I can see the SCIM Group now with members. That should trigger our API key auto-provisioner. If not, a manual reconcile can be kicked. Sam, can you verify if the Hosted API key appears for jane@acme.com?

sam: Jane confirms no API key yet. I've asked for the approval email to issue a temporary key if auto-provision doesn't run. Also asked them to initiate a full SCIM user query we can inspect: curl -u $SCIM_TOKEN: 'https://scim.redwood.com/v2/Users?filter=emails.value eq "jane@acme.com"'

nora-cs: We checked internal logs  the auto-provision job runs every 10m and logs show it tried at 09:50 and skipped because group->role mapping wasn't present until 09:46. There's a race but it should pick up on next run. We'll watch and confirm.

maria: Added to KB: quick checklist for Okta POCs (link): https://redwood.internal/kb/poc-okta-checklist. Key items: SAML metadata exchange, SCIM token + scopes, Push Groups enabled, group naming conventions (rdw_* or acme_poc_*), and approval process for manual keys.

sam: Customer followed up: they prefer SAML group claims instead of push. Asked what claim name we expect.

lee-idp: We accept claim name "groups" or "groupNames" and mapping uses literal group displayName to tenant role mapping. If Okta truncates groups due to token size it will send group by reference; in that case SCIM is required for membership.

okta-bot: Provisioning log: 2024-09-05T10:01:10Z USER_PATCH user=jane@acme.com status=200 groups_attached=1

kevin: Confirmed: auto-provisioner ran at 10:00 and created Hosted API key label="acme-poc-auto-1" for jane@acme.com. Please have Acme rotate and delete after the POC.

sam: I'll collect the approval email anyway and close once they confirm the key works. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
